title: Quarterly OKR synthesis: model tiering commitments & contingency lanes
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary:
Run a coordinated quarterly planning and OKR-synthesis session that produces a single source-of-truth for which models are committed to Hosted API in Q2, how they map to product OKRs, and explicit contingency lanes (fallbacks & capacity hedges) for each commitment. This ticket focuses on alignment, decision criteria, and publishing the final commitment matrix to the Console roadmap and the Model Catalog pages.

Goals:
- Produce a prioritized list of model commitments (green/amber/red) with clear acceptance criteria tied to latency, cost/unit, and quality regressions.
- Define 2 contingency lanes per commitment: (1) capacity hedge (Dedicated/pinned variants) and (2) graceful fallback (compatible model variant or quantized variant).
- Publish a rollout calendar with canary windows, experiment lanes for feature flags, and rollback thresholds.

Scope & Out-of-scope:
- In-scope: Hosted API model lineup for Q2 (text-generation and embeddings), per-model SLO targets, canary window calendar, dependency mapping to infra/engineering work (ENG tickets), and an owner for each lane.
- Out-of-scope: Private/VPC deployment choreography, billing model refactor, and major schema changes to the API surface.

Decision criteria (must include at least one):
1) Latency SLO: p95 for 1k token completion < 300ms for gen-lite tiers, < 700ms for long-context variants.
2) Cost per token: preferred unit cost delta < 1.5x against current baseline for same quality bracket.
3) Quality stability: no more than 1% top-line regression on our ridge evals (conversational and instruction tasks) vs. the incumbent for acceptance.

Deliverables:
- Commitment matrix (CSV + published Console doc) with columns: model, tier, owner, SLOs, evaluation baseline link, contingency lanes, canary start date.
- Rollout calendar (Google Sheet) with blocked windows for infra, canary, and full switch.
- Risk register with mitigation playbooks for: capacity shortfall, regression, and cost overruns.
- Small PRD describing gating signals and automated rollback thresholds for the rollout.

Stakeholders & owners:
- PM lead: Ava Martinez (owner of commitment decisions)
- Infra/Runtime: Priya Nair (ENG-19822)
- Developer Experience (Console): Marco Delgado (DES-324)
- Research / Evals: Dr. Elena Park (evaluation baseline owner)
- Customer Success: Tom Alvarez (customer communications & impact assessment)

Timeline / Milestones:
- 2026-03-05: Kickoff & initial candidate model list (this ticket created).
- 2026-03-08: Evals baseline reports delivered (link below).
- 2026-03-10: Cross-team synthesis workshop + contingency lane draft.
- 2026-03-12: Final commitment vote (PM/ENG/R&D) and publish matrix.
- 2026-03-20 to 2026-04-04: Canary windows per model (scheduled in rollout calendar).

Acceptance criteria:
- Commitment matrix published to the Console roadmap and linked in the Model Catalog Confluence page.
- Each committed model has an assigned contingency lane and an ENG owner with at least one dependency ticket open.
- Canary playbooks and rollback thresholds are documented and approved by Runtime and Evals.

Links & artifacts:
- Candidate model list & eval summaries: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1-example-model-evals
- Draft commitment spreadsheet (editable): https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1-example-rollout-calendar
- PRD (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PM/pages/912468-commitment-prd
- Console roadmap mock: https://console.redwood/internals/roadmap/q2-commitments
- Related ENG ticket (runtime work): ENG-19822

Trade-offs discussed:
- Keeping more models in the lineup improves customer choice but increases operational surface area and regression risk — we bias towards narrower initial commitments with explicit experiment lanes to expand after a stable canary.
- Quantized variants reduce cost but introduce a quality delta; we will allow quantized fallbacks only if ridge eval gap < 0.8% and latency gains > 30%.

Open questions / blockers:
- Need final confirmation on Dedicated capacity reservations (cost approval) by Finance (link to spend request in comments).
- Determining the exact canary sampling fraction for high-traffic endpoints (proposal located in PRD).

Follow-ups after close:
- Schedule post-mortem within two weeks of any canary that triggers rollback.
- Add weekly model health metrics to Console dashboards for the first month after full rollout.

Notes for reviewers:
- Please review the acceptance thresholds and particularly the cost-per-token guardrails. If you think we should tighten or relax a threshold, leave a comment with the rationale and example metrics.
